events.title: Dark Dublin, Dracula, Bram Stoker & Other Horrors
events.description: Bram Stoker may be Ireland's most famous writer worldwide — even rivalling James Joyce, though that's a debate for another day. Building on a lineage of Irish horror writers, Stoker gave the world Dracula, a tale of devilishness that has gripped the global imagination like no other work of fiction. This walk explores Stoker's work against his own era and the millennia of Irish stories of evil spirits and our uneasy pact with the Underworld. A thousand years of foreign occupation left Dublin steeped in blood, fear and persecution — darkness that fed the imagination. We'll revel in his predecessors too: Charles Maturin, Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu, and Oscar Wilde, each conjuring their own vision of the Other World.

events.title: Legends, Ghosts and Ghouls of Dublin | Walking Tour
events.description: Ireland has a unique relationship with its legendary past. Kept alive in the histories of the Filí and the Seanchaidhe, Ireland’s gods were not destroyed but - in the words of Mark Williams - demoted to lesser beings. This is an important element of Ireland’s oral histories, which in turn have coloured its popular histories and left many legends for us to parse over today. On the other side of Irish history we have the ballrooms, the salons, and the private studies of Dublin’s litterati. The seances and unwrapping parties, the mysteries and the macabre, all combining into the secret esoteric orders that strove to unlock the secrets of existence. events.description: Halloween night begins at The Lark with one of cinema’s earliest and most memorable monsters. Released in 1920, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde stars John Barrymore as the respectable doctor whose experiments to separate the good and evil within himself unleash the sinister Mr. Hyde. More than a century later, Barrymore’s remarkable transformation remains one of the great performances of early horror cinema. Start Halloween with a 100-year-old tale of science, temptation and the monster within, experienced as cinema should be: on the big screen, together, in the darkness of a theatre. events.title: Halloween & its Creepy Irish Origins
events.description: Want a chilling experience? Not too chilling — we want you entertained, not terrified. But we do venture into the supernatural and the origins behind Halloween customs we still enjoy today. Halloween began as a Christian overlay on the ancient Irish feast of Samhain. The Celts revered their ancestors — and feared them too. On this night, the veil between worlds thinned and spirits, mostly malevolent, walked the land. People devised tactics to protect themselves, customs that survive today as Halloween traditions. Irish writers drew on this folklore for their own spectral creations — The Picture of Dorian Gray, Melmoth the Wanderer, Carmilla, and Dracula. We'll dip into it all, and try not to get splashed in blood!

events.description: You might know it as Halloween, but the origins of this carnival of all things supernatural lie deep within our Celtic roots – traditions such as trick or treat, apple bobbing and jack o’lanterns were all part of Samhain, the pagan Harvest-time celebration of All Hallow’s Eve. Join us in a musical celebration of this ancient Irish festival - and indulge our continuing love for all things ghoulish, ghostly and chilling of the spine.
